title: Reading rewards.py: two graders in under 100 lines

steps.title: The three patterns
steps.markdown: Everything starts with three search patterns (regular expressions). `FORMAT_PATTERN` describes the whole shape we want: optional spaces, a `<think>` block, then an `<answer>` block, and nothing else. `ANSWER_PATTERN` grabs whatever sits between the answer tags. `NUMBER_PATTERN` finds numbers like `18`, `-3` or `2.5`. `re.DOTALL` lets the dot match line breaks, because real thinking spans many lines.

steps.title: Two shapes of completion
steps.markdown: TRL hands your reward function either plain strings or, for chat-style datasets, a list of messages like `[{"role": "assistant", "content": "..."}]`. `completion_text` turns both into a plain string, so every other function only has to think about text.

steps.title: Finding the gold answer and the model's answer
steps.markdown: GSM8K writes the worked solution first and the final number after `####`. `gold_from_gsm8k` keeps only that number. `extract_answer` returns what the model put inside `<answer>`, or `None` if the tags are missing. Returning `None` instead of crashing matters: early in training most answers are messy.

steps.title: Forgiving number parsing
steps.markdown: Models write `18`, `$18.`, `18 dollars` or `1,200`. `parse_number` removes commas and keeps the last number it finds, so all of those count. This is a design choice: we grade the number, not the decoration around it.

steps.title: The strict format reward
steps.markdown: One line: 1.0 if the whole completion matches the pattern, 0.0 otherwise. Notice the `**kwargs`. TRL passes extra arguments (prompts, dataset columns, and more), and accepting them with `**kwargs` keeps your function from crashing when it receives ones it does not use.

steps.title: Partial credit for format
steps.markdown: A brand new model almost never produces the perfect shape, so a strict reward gives it nothing to learn from. `soft_format_reward` gives 0.25 for each tag that appears exactly once, which hands out small steps toward the target. Partial credit helps learning get started, but every extra rule is also a new thing the model can game.

steps.title: The correctness reward
steps.markdown: `answer` is a column in the dataset, so TRL passes it in by name. For each completion we parse the model's number and the gold number and compare them with a tiny tolerance (`1e-6`), so `18.0` and `18` count as equal. If either side cannot be parsed, the score is 0.

steps.title: Adding the scores together
steps.markdown: `total_reward` shows what the trainer does when you pass several reward functions: it adds them up (TRL can also weight them with `reward_weights`). Here correctness is worth 1.0 and format 0.5, so being right always beats being tidy.

steps.title: The demo, and a loophole
steps.markdown: Run `python rewards.py` to grade six sample answers. Look closely at the `tags twice` row: the strict format reward still gives it 1.0, because the lazy `.+?` can stretch across the extra tags to reach the end. The soft reward catches it. Finding holes like this before training is exactly the job of this lab.
